latest_release.name: v3.5.0
latest_release.body:
Dear preCICE community,

We are happy to announce a new preCICE release v3.5.0.

This release adds support for conservative PU-RBF mappings via Kokkos and exporters can now define which mesh to export `<export:vtu mesh="Fluid" />`. The latter can significantly reduce required storage when exporting iterations in a multi-mesh setup.

Some improvements have been made to mesh filtering and merging operations, which improve runtime and memory consumption of the initialization of parallel solvers. Furthermore, the comparison of timestamps is now more robust, allowing longer-running simulations.

Noteworthy bug fixes include CMake no longer linking Boost.Test against libprecice and no longer requiring it if tests are disabled. Support for linking to a static build of Boost has also been disabled, as this is incompatible with Boost.Log.

With the recent Ubuntu 26.04 LTS release, this version of preCICE now lifts the baseline to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, dropping support for previous versions.
The version is compatible and tested with Clang 23.1.4, GCC 16.2.1, Boost 1.92.0, libxml2 2.15.4, and Eigen 5.0.1.

For the highlights, read the blog post(todo).
For all details, check the full list of changes in the [changelog](https://github.com/precice/precice/blob/v3.5.0/CHANGELOG.md).

Happy coupling!
